title: Energy Settlement Working Basis — Arriving at a Downside Protection Credit
content:
Downside protection credited on a pre-buy booking held on an account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts is worked out on the gallons the member has booked and not yet drawn on the account, measured against the posted price for the product.

A will-call stop is one the records show the member called in, and not one run to the automatic keep-full schedule, run as an emergency, run after hours or made to fill against a booking.

## The quantities, in the order they are settled

1. **The gallons still undrawn** are the gallons booked on the account less the gallons already drawn against those bookings, and nothing is held back from them.
2. **The rack of record** is the price billed on the most recent will-call stop, less the programme's posted price margin.
3. **The margin allowed on the account** is the programme's posted price margin.
4. **The posted price** is the rack of record plus the margin allowed on the account, taken to four decimal places.
5. **The protected floor** is the programme's floor percentage of the price the gallons were booked at, taken to four decimal places.
6. **The credit per gallon** is the protected floor less the posted price, and where the posted price stands at or above the protected floor the credit per gallon is nothing.
7. **The protection set against the credit.** Nothing already credited is set against the credit.
8. **The credit** is the gallons still undrawn multiplied by the credit per gallon, less the protection set against it, and the whole of it is rounded to two decimal places once at the end and never falls below nothing.

Both the posted price and the protected floor are taken to four decimal places before the credit per gallon is arrived at; the rounding to two decimal places is done once, on the credit as a whole, after the protection has been set against it.

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

Take a booking on the Contract Gallon Pre-Buy Account, whose catalogue floor percentage is 90 percent and whose posted price margin is 0.80 USD per gallon. Suppose the account carries 1000.0 gallons booked and 300.0 gallons drawn against those bookings; the most recent will-call stop was billed at 2.0000 USD per gallon; and the gallons were booked at 2.4000 USD per gallon.

- Gallons still undrawn: 1000.0 less 300.0, coming to 700.0 gallons.
- Rack of record: 2.0000 less the margin of 0.8000, coming to 1.2000 USD per gallon.
- Margin allowed on the account: 0.8000 USD per gallon.
- Posted price: 1.2000 plus 0.8000, coming to 2.0000 USD per gallon.
- Protected floor: 90 percent of 2.4000, coming to 2.1600 USD per gallon.
- Credit per gallon: 2.1600 less 2.0000, coming to 0.1600 USD per gallon, which is above nothing and so stands.
- Credit: 700.0 gallons multiplied by 0.1600, coming to 112.00 USD, with nothing set against it.

Had the posted price come out at 2.2000 USD per gallon instead, it would stand above the protected floor of 2.1600, the credit per gallon would be nothing, and the credit would come to 0.00 USD.
